1.2 Coherences

So far, we have introduced functors and their identifications, but we have essentially no relations between them. We next specify the coherence relations we will use. We first describe composition of identifications and its compatibility with whiskering. We then introduce the unit and associativity identifications for composition of functors, and the relations among them.

For readability, we write most of these coherences in their ‘term notation’, cf. Notation 1.1.3. In each case, the axiom introduces a specified identification of functors, which we will often leave nameless to avoid cluttering of notation.

1.2.1 Composition of identifications

Identifications can be composed: given identifications \(\sigma :f=g\) and \(\tau :g=h\), we obtain an identification \(\tau \circ \sigma :f=h\). We call this vertical composition to distinguish it from the horizontal composition introduced below. Every functor has an identity identification, and every identification has an inverse.

Axiom A.3 (Composition of identifications). For every functor \(f\), there is an identity identification \(\id _f\colon f= f\). For parallel functors \(f,g,h\colon C\to D\), there is a composition functor \[ -\circ -\colon (g= h)\times (f= g)\longrightarrow (f= h). \] There is also an inverse functor \[ (-)^{-1}\colon (f=g)\to (g=f). \] This composition is unital and associative, and the inverse functor supplies two-sided inverses, through specified identifications of functors on the corresponding animae of identifications. For \(\alpha :f=g\), \(\beta :g=h\), and \(\gamma :h=k\), where \(k\colon C\to D\), these laws read \[ \id _g\circ \alpha =\alpha ,\qquad \alpha \circ \id _f=\alpha , \] \[ (\gamma \circ \beta )\circ \alpha =\gamma \circ (\beta \circ \alpha ), \] \[ \alpha ^{-1}\circ \alpha =\id _f,\qquad \alpha \circ \alpha ^{-1}=\id _g. \]

Supporting result: isoComp-assoc-left

isoComp-assoc-left

Derivation, checked

  isoComp-assoc-left : {C D : CAT} (f g h k : MAP C D)
    → let X = ((h ＝ k) × (g ＝ h)) × (f ＝ g)
          α : MAP X (f ＝ g)
          α = pr₂
          β : MAP X (g ＝ h)
          β = pr₂ ∘ pr₁
          γ : MAP X (h ＝ k)
          γ = pr₁ ∘ pr₁
      in ((γ ∙ β) ∙ α) =₁ (γ ∙ (β ∙ α))
Proof / implementation
  isoComp-assoc-left f g h k =
    let γ = pr₁ ∘ pr₁
        β = pr₂ ∘ pr₁
        α = pr₂
        r = pair γ (pair β α)
        first = pair-β₁ γ (pair β α)
        second = pair-β₁ β α ∙ ((pr₁ ◁ pair-β₂ γ (pair β α)) ∙ comp-assoc r pr₂ pr₁)
        third = pair-β₂ β α ∙ ((pr₂ ◁ pair-β₂ γ (pair β α)) ∙ comp-assoc r pr₂ pr₂)
    in specialize (isoComp-assoc f g h k) r
      (isoComp-evaluate (pr₁ ∙ (pr₁ ∘ pr₂)) (pr₂ ∘ pr₂) r
        (isoComp-evaluate pr₁ (pr₁ ∘ pr₂) r first second) third)
      (isoComp-evaluate pr₁ ((pr₁ ∘ pr₂) ∙ (pr₂ ∘ pr₂)) r first
        (isoComp-evaluate (pr₁ ∘ pr₂) (pr₂ ∘ pr₂) r second third))

isoComp-assoc-at

Derivation, checked

  isoComp-assoc-at : {C D : CAT} {f g h k : MAP C D}
    (γ : h =₁ k) (β : g =₁ h) (α : f =₁ g)
    → ((γ ∙ β) ∙ α) =₂ (γ ∙ (β ∙ α))
Proof / implementation
  isoComp-assoc-at {f = f} {g} {h} {k} γ β α =
    let open TriplePoint γ β α
    in specialize (isoComp-assoc-left f g h k) point
      (isoComp-evaluate ((pr₁ ∘ pr₁) ∙ (pr₂ ∘ pr₁)) pr₂ point
        (isoComp-evaluate (pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (pr₂ ∘ pr₁) point first second) third)
      (isoComp-evaluate (pr₁ ∘ pr₁) ((pr₂ ∘ pr₁) ∙ pr₂) point first
        (isoComp-evaluate (pr₂ ∘ pr₁) pr₂ point second third))

The displayed laws are specified identifications of functors on the relevant animae of inputs. For parallel functors \(f,g,h,k\colon C\to D\), the associativity law compares the two functors \[ (h=k)\times \bigl ((g=h)\times (f=g)\bigr )\longrightarrow (f=k) \] given by \((\gamma ,(\beta ,\alpha ))\mapsto (\gamma \circ \beta )\circ \alpha \) and \((\gamma ,(\beta ,\alpha ))\mapsto \gamma \circ (\beta \circ \alpha )\). Precomposing these comparisons with a functor into the input anima gives the same laws for the resulting expressions.

We can now also speak of commutative squares, triangles, and more general diagrams of identifications, using the convention of Definition 1.1.4 with vertical composition along their boundaries.

1.2.2 Whiskering and horizontal composition

Whiskering composes an identification with a functor on either side. We first require that it respect identity identifications and vertical composition.

Axiom A.4 (Whiskering and vertical composition). Prewhiskering and postwhiskering preserve identity identifications and vertical composition through specified identifications of functors on the input animae of identifications. For functors \(f,g,h\colon C\to D\), \(k\colon B\to C\) and \(u\colon D\to E\), these laws read \[ u\star \id _f=\id _{u\circ f},\qquad \id _f\star k=\id _{f\circ k}, \] \[ u\star (\tau \circ \sigma ) =(u\star \tau )\circ (u\star \sigma ),\qquad (\tau \circ \sigma )\star k =(\tau \star k)\circ (\sigma \star k), \] where \(\sigma \colon f= g\) and \(\tau \colon g= h\). The two vertical-composition comparisons are identifications of functors on \((g=h)\times (f=g)\).

Agda Whiskering preserves identities

Given identifications \(\tau :F=G\) and \(\sigma :h=k\), where \(F,G\colon D\to E\) and \(h,k\colon T\to D\), there are two ways to obtain an identification \(Fh=Gk\): one can first change \(h\) to \(k\), or first change \(F\) to \(G\). The interchange rule compares these two constructions.

Axiom A.5 (Interchange). The two ways of pasting identifications are identified. More precisely, for \(\tau \colon F= G\) with \(F,G\colon D\to E\) and \(h,k\colon T\to D\), there is an identification of functors \((h= k)\to (Fh= Gk)\) \[ (\tau \star k)\circ (F\star -) \ =\ (G\star -)\circ (\tau \star h). \] Here composition with a fixed identification uses it as a constant input. Likewise, for fixed \(\sigma \colon h= k\), the two functors \((F= G)\to (Fh= Gk)\) given by \[ (-\star k)\circ (F\star \sigma ) \quad \text {and}\quad (G\star \sigma )\circ (-\star h) \] are identified.

Agda Interchange with a fixed input

      → let σ = id (h ＝ k)
        in (const (τ ▷ k) ∙ (F ◁ σ)) =₁ ((G ◁ σ) ∙ const (τ ▷ h))

Given \(\alpha \colon f= f'\) and \(\beta \colon g= g'\), we write \[ \beta \ast \alpha :=(\beta \star f')\circ (g\star \alpha ): gf= g'f' \] for their horizontal composite. Interchange compares this with \((g'\star \alpha )\circ (\beta \star f)\). In particular, horizontal composition preserves identities and vertical composites. For fixed functors \(f,f',g,g'\), this construction defines a functor \[ - \ast - \colon (g = g') \times (f = f') \to (gf = g'f'). \]

hcomp-isoComp-family {f₁ = f₁} {f₂} {g₀ = g₀} {g₁} β₂ β₁ α₂ α₁ =

      γ = β₁ ▷ f₂

1.2.3 Units and associativity of functor composition

Composition of functors is unital and associative through specified identifications, called the unitors and associator.

Axiom A.6 (Unitors and associator). For functors \(f\colon C\to D\), \(g\colon D\to E\) and \(h\colon E\to F\), there are identifications \[ \lambda _f\colon \id _D\circ f= f,\qquad \rho _f\colon f\circ \id _C= f,\qquad \alpha _{f,g,h}\colon (h\circ g)\circ f= h\circ (g\circ f). \]

  • For identifications \(\alpha \colon f = f'\), \(\beta \colon g = g'\) and \(\gamma \colon h = h'\), the following square of identifications commutes:

    Agda Horizontal associativity comparison

    hcomp-assoc

    Assumption, type checked

        hcomp-assoc : {B C D E : CAT} (f f′ : MAP B C) (g g′ : MAP C D) (h h′ : MAP D E)
      → let X = ((h ＝ h′) × (g ＝ g′)) × (f ＝ f′)
            α : MAP X (f ＝ f′)
            α = pr₂
            β : MAP X (g ＝ g′)
            β = pr₂ ∘ pr₁
            γ : MAP X (h ＝ h′)
            γ = pr₁ ∘ pr₁
        in (const (comp-assoc f′ g′ h′) ∙ ((γ ⋆ β) ⋆ α)) =₁
                  ((γ ⋆ (β ⋆ α)) ∙ const (comp-assoc f g h))

    postWhisker-comp

    Derivation, checked

      postWhisker-comp : {C D E F : CAT} (f g : MAP C D) (u : MAP D E) (v : MAP E F)
    → let σ = id (f ＝ g)
      in (const (comp-assoc g u v) ∙ ((v ∘ u) ◁ σ)) =₁
        ((v ◁ (u ◁ σ)) ∙ const (comp-assoc f u v))
    Proof / implementation
      postWhisker-comp f g u v =
    let σ = id (f ＝ g)
        left = horizontal-identityˡ (v ∘ u) σ ∙
          hcomp-cong (horizontal-identities u v) (idIso σ)
        right = (postWhisker v ◁ horizontal-identityˡ u σ) ∙
          horizontal-identityˡ v (const (idIso u) ⋆ σ)
    in isoComp-cong right (idIso (const (comp-assoc f u v))) ∙
      (horizontal-assoc (const (idIso v)) (const (idIso u)) σ ∙
        (isoComp-cong (idIso (const (comp-assoc g u v))) left) ⁻¹)

These comparisons are identifications of the corresponding functors on products of the input animae of identifications. Their restrictions along functors into those animae give the same formulas for identifications.

Remark 1.2.1. Taking some of the input identifications to be identities gives compatibility with identifications in each individual functor.

It will sometimes be convenient to abbreviate the conditions from Axiom A.7 as follows: \[ \id \ast \alpha = \alpha = \alpha \ast \id \qquadtext { and } (\gamma \ast \beta ) \ast \alpha = \gamma \ast (\beta \ast \alpha ). \] More generally, if we are given identifications \(\alpha \colon f = g\) and \(\alpha ' \colon f' = g'\) of functors \(C \to D\), and we happen to be given identifications \(f = f'\) and \(g = g'\), we will write \(\alpha = \alpha '\) to indicate the existence of a commutative square of identifications as follows:

Agda Comparison squares with different endpoints

NatIsoSquare

Definition, checked

record NatIsoSquare {C D : CAT} (f g f′ g′ : MAP C D) : Set m where
  field
    top : f =₁ g
    bottom : f′ =₁ g′
    left : f =₁ f′
    right : g =₁ g′
    cell : (right ∙ top) =₂ (bottom ∙ left)

1.2.4 The pentagon and triangle identities

Finally, the unitors and associator must themselves be compatible. The pentagon compares the two ways of reassociating a composite of four functors. The triangle compares removing an identity functor before or after reassociation.

Axiom A.8 (Pentagon and triangle identities). For functors \(f\colon A \to B\), \(g\colon B \to C\), \(h\colon C \to D\) and \(k\colon D \to E\), the following pentagon of identifications commutes:

Agda The pentagon

comp-pentagon

Assumption, type checked

    comp-pentagon : {A B C D E : CAT} (f : MAP A B) (g : MAP B C)
      (h : MAP C D) (k : MAP D E)
      → let short = comp-assoc (g ∘ f) h k ∙ comp-assoc f g (k ∘ h)
            long = ((idIso k ⋆ comp-assoc f g h) ∙ comp-assoc f (h ∘ g) k)
                   ∙ (comp-assoc g h k ⋆ idIso f)
        in short =₂ long
